decisions.decision: A real 0.0 tyre delta renders NO icon but still prints its numeric line ('0.0 vs prev. day'). A nil delta prints no line at all. No third neutral glyph is added.
decisions.why: User picked it from three options. The numeric line already tells 'no change' apart from 'unknown', so a new glyph in the shared ui/ kit is not worth the blast radius.

decisions.decision: Tier 4 touches no database object, so the built-in database design gate does not apply. It reads the same precomputed row tier 3 already widened.
decisions.why: The gate exists for schema changes. Recording the check so a reviewer sees it was made, not skipped.

review.brief: Review commits eff7117 and 0ba946d on ft/RM50-MAG-56-vehicle-status-subsections against openspec/changes/RM50-gateway-add-tire-pressure-subsection/{design.md,specs/gateway/spec.md,tasks.md}. Check: (1) RD14 -- a real 0.0 delta renders NO icon but DOES render its numeric line; a nil delta renders neither. This is the owner's own decision and the highest-value check. Verify it in dashTireTrend/dashTireDelta AND in the tests. (2) RD11 -- the panel reuses ui.StatTileProps.Trend and the existing trending_up/trending_down glyphs. A second trend mechanism, or a new glyph, is a blocker finding. (3) The tests assert design.md's Test Contract fixtures, authored before implementation -- not whatever the code happens to do. (4) RD8 -- no cosmetic tests: nothing coupled to markup, CSS classes, ARIA or element placement. (5) RD6 -- no hardcoded colour; semantic theme tokens only. (6) i18n -- all seven new keys have non-empty ES and EN, and no user-facing string bypasses i18n.T. (7) Boundaries -- nothing outside internal/gateway except the two named KB files and this change's artifacts; no new query and no new analytics call, the panel reads the one precomputed row. (8) Anti-gaming: no weakened or deleted criteria, no self-approved status; tasks.md matches reality. (9) No HTML comments in markup. (10) Docs track the change, and openspec/changes/archive/ is untouched. SIGNAL PROVENANCE: go build, go vet, ui-guard, i18n-guard, archive-guard, boundary-guard and a templ/css idempotency check were ASSISTANT-run and clean. The suite was run by the OWNER, who reported `make test` and `make check` passing. Do NOT run the suite. Judge test quality by reading the tests. KNOWN AND OUT OF SCOPE: gofmt -l flags internal/gateway/vehicle_image_test.go. It is pre-existing drift, untouched by these commits. Do not raise it as a finding.

checks.note: dashTireTrend(v) returns "" for nil AND for *v==0; dashTireDelta(v) returns "" only for nil, formats a real 0.0 as "0.0 vs prev. day". ui.StatTile only renders the Desc line when non-empty (stat_tile.templ), so an empty Delta truly renders nothing. Confirmed in both dashTireTrend/dashTireDelta and the FixtureFull test (RL wheel: Trend "", Delta "0.0 vs prev. day"; RR wheel nil/nil: Trend "", Delta "").

dashTireWheel sets fragments.TireWheelVM.Trend to "up"/"down"/"", passed straight into ui.StatTileProps.Trend in dashboard.templ. statTrendIcon (stat_tile.templ) switches on trending_up/trending_down, both pre-existing from tier 2 (icon.templ). No new glyph, no hand-written arrow, no second mechanism.

handlers_test.go fixture values (42.06/0.4, 40.6/-0.3, 39.2/0.0, nil/nil) and expected strings match design.md's Test Contract table verbatim, authored before implementation. Verified arithmetic myself: 42.06 -> "42.1 PSI" (rounds up correctly), formatSignedPSI(0.4)="+0.4", (-0.3)="-0.3", (0.0)="0.0" (no sign) -- all correct.

Only additions are to TestMapDashboardSnapshot_FixtureFull/FixtureNil, pure Go struct-field assertions on fragments.TireWheelVM. No markup, CSS class, ARIA, or placement assertion anywhere in the diff.
grep for "231 189 184" and "rgb(" across every touched file returns nothing. dashboard.templ uses only ui.SectionHeader/ui.StatTile; no inline class.
Seven new keys (KeyDashboardTirePressureTitle/Desc, KeyDashboardTireFL/FR/RL/RR, KeyDashboardTireDeltaDesc), all with non-empty ES and EN on the same line in catalog.go. make i18n-guard passed clean.
